findings.message: parseGitHubUrl matches the branch segment but throws it away, so resolveIdentifier always uses the repo's default branch instead. `spm install https://github.com/org/repo/tree/develop/path/to/skill` fetches skillset.yml and every file from `main`. That either 404s or quietly installs the wrong version. Branches with a slash (`tree/feature/x/claude/skill`) also get split wrong: `feature` is taken as the branch and `x/claude/skill` as the path.

downloadEntries builds every GitHubSource with location.ref, including cross-repo (@owner/repo/path) entries whose owner/repository differ from the skillset's repo. The skillset lives in a repo whose default branch is `main` and references `@other/lib/skills/x`, where `other/lib` only has `master`. Every cross-repo file download fails with a 404 from raw.githubusercontent.com, so the whole install aborts.

The path-traversal guard uses a bare `startsWith(baseDir)` with no trailing separator, and baseDir itself comes from `skillset.name`, which is never validated. A manifest with `name: ../../../Users/<author>/.ssh` makes `join(tmpdir(),'spm',name)` resolve outside tmp, and safePath then accepts any file under it, so the attacker writes arbitrary files. Separately, with name `fsd`, a file entry `../fsd-evil/x` resolves to `/tmp/spm/fsd-evil/x`, which passes `startsWith('/tmp/spm/fsd')`.

Files are written to tmpDir/entry.path without the owner or repository, so same-path files from different repos (cross-repo sources) overwrite each other in a concurrent Promise.all. The skillset repo and a cross-repo source both have `skills/git/SKILL.md`. Both writes target the same file at the same time, and whichever finishes last silently wins. The success message still reports both files as downloaded.

The URL regex captures the path including a trailing slash, and resolveIdentifier then appends `/skillset.yml`, producing a double slash. `https://github.com/org/repo/tree/main/claude/skill/` yields path `claude/skill/`, so the code fetches `claude/skill//skillset.yml`. The manifest fetch fails or the derived skillsetDir is wrong.
